title: Bearer header fragmentation - scratchpad
content:
Quick brain-dump on a weird class of 401/429s that seem correlated with large Authorization headers and intermittent proxies. Putting steps, logs, hypotheses, and quick repro notes here so I don't forget.

Summary / symptom:
- Several customers (mobile SDK + server-side proxy) report intermittent 401s and 429s for the same client key within seconds of successful requests.
- Errors are bursty and tend to happen when client requests include additional metadata in the Bearer header (custom claims encoded into token or long JWTs) or when requests pass through an edge proxy that performs header parsing.
- Not consistent across all regions; more frequent through APAC edge node pool.

Concrete error snippets seen in logs:
- 401 response body: "{"error":"unauthorized","detail":"invalid_auth_header"}"
- 429 response body: "{"error":"rate_exceeded","quota_window":"unknown"}"
- Upstream ingress logs: "v=1 t=2026-02-28T15:12:43Z peer=10.0.2.5 method=POST path=/v1/generate auth_len=1024 parsed_auth=truncated"
- Envoy access log (edge): "HTTP/1.1 401  0  0  -  r=0.003"

Commands / quick repro attempts:
- curl simple happy path (works):
  curl -s -D - -H "Authorization: Bearer $SHORT_TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/complete -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'

- curl with long fake header (intermittent fail locally when routing through local nginx):
  LONG=\$(python3 -c "print('A'*3500)")
  curl -s -D - -H "Authorization: Bearer $LONG" -X POST https://local-edge:8443/v1/complete -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'

- tcpdump of failing request between client and proxy: captured, header arrives chunked (Transfer-Encoding: chunked) and Authorization header split across two TCP segments.

Observations:
- When header length > ~2048 bytes, some proxies (old nginx + http2 middleboxes) appear to reject or truncate the header silently, causing our parser to see a malformed/short auth token -> 401.
- Some 429s appear with identical tokens — hypothesis: truncated header leads to hash mismatches in our quota key (we index quota by token string), so truncated vs full token counts as different clients. If truncated string maps to hot key, rate limiter fires 429 for that truncated key while full token has no usage.
- Timing: bursts align with SDKs that embed additional context (session metadata) inside JWTs and then rotate rapidly (client re-issues tokens every ~10s). The rotation + truncated-string behavior may cause a thundering set of distinct truncated keys hitting rate limits on the edge.
- Not all edges show same behavior: older edge VMs have a known header-buffer-size lower default.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) proxy/header fragmentation: edge proxies break long Authorization header across frames and some intermediates truncate or normalize header wrongly -> leads to malformed token -> 401 or unexpected quota-key variants -> 429.
2) client library re-encoding: certain http client (mobile) sets header as list of strings or uses chunked transfer encoding causing server parsing differences.
3) header size limit on load balancer: LB returns 401 for oversized header rather than 431, and our client interprets as auth failure.
4) race in token rotation: overlapping tokens cause quota window distribution weirdness; not primary but amplifies problem.

Logs to gather (actionable):
- full raw request capture (tcpdump) at client -> proxy and proxy -> ingress for failing window.
- envoy/httpd/nginx config for APAC edge nodes: client_header_buffer_size, large_client_header_buffers, http2 settings.
- compare Access-Log raw header values (obfuscated) when failure vs success.
- quota key generation logs in rate-limiter: log token string length and prefix hash when returning 429.

Quick experiments to run (locally & staging):
- reproduce with python requests and chunked encoding on local nginx gateway; toggle client_header_buffer_size from 1k -> 8k.
- modify SDK to strip optional metadata from token (shorten) and confirm error rate drops.
- force upstream to accept oversized headers (envoy config) and measure failure count.
- run variant where we compute quota key from header fingerprint (e.g., HMAC of full header) and log collisions.

Immediate mitigations (temporary):
- Add debug logging: when 401/429 occurs, log len(auth_header) and first/last 8 chars (redact middle) and origin-edge id.
- Add guarded fallback: if parsed authorization looks malformed, attempt to reconstruct from raw header fragments (only in internal staging) before rejecting.
- Communication: ping mobile SDK owners to stop embedding large metadata in JWTs; recommend short-lived claims stored server-side.

Next steps / todo:
- [ ] Capture live tcpdump during next customer burst (coordinate with customer windows)
- [ ] Instrument rate-limiter to increment metric for "short-token-429" when token length < expected_threshold and 429 is returned
- [ ] Inspect APAC edge nginx/envoy config and compare with NA
- [ ] Prepare small PR to add auth_header length logging and a feature-flagged tolerant parse path
- [ ] Draft note to SDK owners describing safe token length and recommended rotation cadence

Notes to self:
- Be careful not to log full tokens; always redact middle. Use prefix(8)+suffix(8).
- If this is a proxy problem, fix upstream; if an SRE config issue, escalate to infra.

End of scratch. Will paste tcpdump + truncated hex dump below when I capture it.
